nextExecutableAction: Lead consumes this preflight and supplies the committed wave0 revision plus root-accepted RS-DRV-01 and RS-DOC-01 integration receipts with actual registry/selection, CRDT owner/WAL, independent File/source ACL and migration contracts. Revalidate every affected whole-file hash against that input, resolve FG-NATIVE-EXTERNAL-PUBLISH, and freeze command/preview/receipt types. Then dispatch RS-NOTE-01 implementation in dependency order: personal Drive projection/stable aliases first, reviewed shared cutover second. Worker implementation ownership remains the two normative UI files; lead integrates all shared patch requests and verifies full DoD. No feature implementation starts from this preflight alone.
risks: Uncommitted root wave0 is live and may change these hashes/seams before integration; the published source snapshot must not overwrite the newer commitMarkdown mechanism.

Filesystem lease safety for cooperating writers is not universal external-editor CAS; [INFERENCE] a non-participating write can race the final check/rename interval unless a real publication contract addresses it.
Path-derived IDs and first-match wiki titles can select the wrong note, remount the editor or detach old aliases. Canonical page/note kind conversion alone is not stable native identity.
Installing a descriptor or flipping UI mode without recoverable owner conversion creates dual writers or stranded drafts. Hardcoded authorityEpoch=1 must not survive shared cutover composition.
Independent image/base64/wiki/mail source privacy is not solved by sharing only the parent Note. Review must prevent embedded bytes, names, URLs, export and cached agent context leaks.
Disposable vault-index recovery patterns can destroy authoritative offline state if reused for docWAL; unsupported schema stamping/wipe is specifically forbidden.
Current in-memory renderer replay state is not evidence of durable shared offline recovery, server ACK-after-persist or current-policy replay.

Scoped preflight cannot certify uninspected global agent tool bypasses, cache reset/upgrade callers, bridge callsites or Page regression behavior. These require exact lead-owned seams and acceptance receipts before full DoD can pass.

Published feature requires real Linux fixture, service, Electron-native and provider readback evidence plus caught seeded assertions. Source inspection, mocked APIs, source-string tests or timeout errors cannot substitute for those gates.
